1. Introduction
Reconstructions of Pangea during late Paleozoic to Mesozoic times indicate that a series of continental
blocks rifted from the northern margin of Gondwana, drifted through the Tethys Ocean and eventually
accretedintoEurasia(Metcalfe,2013;Torsviketal.,2012).Paleomagneticallyquantifyingtherift‐drifthis-
tory of the Gondwana‐derived blocks can provide critical information for understanding their paleo‐
geographiclinkages,whichareessentialtoreconstructtheevolutionoftheTethysOcean.Thoughgeologic
andpaleomagneticdatahavealsobeenobtainedfromtheAlpine(VanDerVoo,2005),Iranian(Besseetal.,
1998;Muttonietal.,2009),Pakistan(Haag&Heller,1991),andPamirs(Xiaoetal.,2005)areas,ourunder-
standingontheevolutionofPaleo‐Tethyshasbeenlargelydominatedbyevidencesfortheearlyformationof
Tibetan Plateau and Southeast Asia peninsula. However, the nature of the linkage between Tibetan and
SoutheastAsianBlocksvariesbetweendifferentmodels.
IntheTibetanarea,theQiangtangBlockisgenerallyconsideredtobesuturedbytheJinshajiangsuturetothe
northandBangong‐Nujiangsuturetothesouth(Roydenetal.,2008;Yin&Harrison,2000),thoughithasalso
beensuggestedtosubdivideintotheNorthQiangtangandSouthQiangtangalongtheLongmuCo‐Shuanghu
suture(Figure1a;Metcalfe,2013;Xuetal.,2015;Lietal.,2016).ThelinkageoftheQiangtangBlockwiththe
SoutheastAsiaBlockscanbecategorizedintotwotypesofmodels:First,theQiangtangBlock,asawhole,
extendssoutheastwardandconnectswiththeSimao‐Indochina(Gehrelsetal.,2011)orBaoshan‐Sibumasu
Block(vanHinsbergenetal.,2011).Second,theNorthQiangtang‐Qamdo‐Simao‐Indochinaisanentireter-
©2019.AmericanGeophysicalUnion.

Tobetterunderstand the linkages betweenthe Tibetan andSoutheastAsia Blocks,we haveconducted a
paleomagnetic and geochronologic study in the southern Lancangjiang Triassic volcanic belt in western
YunnanofChina.ThesouthernLancangjiangTriassicvolcanicbeltrecordsvolcanicactivitiesduringthe
closureofPaleo‐Tethys,asuturezonenowlocatedbetweentheBaoshanandSimaoBlocks.Wesynthesize
ournewdatawithreportedpaleomagnetic,geochemical,geochronological,andsedimentaryevidencesfrom
thePaleo‐Tethysrealmandprovideacomprehensivereconstructionofthepaleogeographicconfigurationof
thisregion.

4. Paleomagnetic Analyses
4.1. DemagnetizationResults
Followingpetrographicandrockmagneticanalyses(TextS3andFiguresS3andS4inthesupportinginfor-
mation),ChRMswithdualpolaritywereisolatedfrom21outofthe23samplingsites,ofwhich11sitescame
fromtheNuozhadurhyolitesand10sitesfromtheXiaodingxivolcanoclasticrocks(TableS1).Forrhyolites
specimens,high‐temperaturecomponentsdecreasestraightforwardlytotheoriginpointfollowingremoval
ofaverylow‐temperaturecomponentby150°C.Morethan80%ofthenaturalremanentmagnetizationswas
onlyerasedbetween660°Cand700°Cwithastep‐spacingof5°C,yieldingstableChRMscarriedbyhematite
(FiguresS5a–S5e).Inthevolcanoclasticrockspecimens,asillustratedinFiguresS5f,S5g,andS5i,following
removal of the low‐temperature components below 400°C, continuous unblocking above 400°C yields
ChRMsrecordedbybothmagnetiteandhematite.

5. Discussions
5.1. LateTriassicPositionofthePaleo‐TethysSutureZoneinWesternYunnan
FollowingtheU‐Pbdatingonzircons,petrographic,rockmagnetic,andpaleomagneticanalyses,wecon-
cludethatthemeanpole(46.1°N/176.2°E,K=44.9,A =4.8°,N=21)derivedfromthevirtualgeomagnetic
95
poles of 21 sites in this study is a robust paleomagnetic data with tight age constraint (approximately
235–230Ma,CarnianAgeofLateTriassic).Thehigh‐qualitydatafulfillallthesevenVanderVoo's(1990)
reliabilitycriteria.Thecorrespondingpaleolatitudeatthereferencesite(23.0°N/100.4°E)inthesouthern
Lancangjiangareais26.0±4.8°NandimpliesthatthepaleomagneticdataobtainedfromtheYiwanshui
FormationinMojiang(Huang&Opdyke,2016)areverylikelyanunderestimate(approximately16.8°N)
of the Late Triassic paleolatitude of the Simao‐Indochina Block. Taking the lithologic property (purplish
red or dark purple mudstones and muddy sandstones) and the elongate distribution of the magnetic
directionsasshowninHuangandOpdyke(2016)intoconsideration,anempiricallybasedflatteningfactor
f=0.6(Torsviketal.,2012;VanderVooetal.,2015)isutilizedtocorrecttheinclinationshallowingbiasfor
thedataoftheYiwanshuiFormation.Thecorrectedinclination(45.3°)andpaleolatitude(26.8°N)agreewell
withthevolcanic‐deriveddatainthisstudy(Figure3a).
IntheperspectiveofLateTriassicpaleogeography,theIndochinaandNorthQiangtangBlocksareinter-
pretedtohavebeenlocatedat29.0±7.2°Nand31.7±3.0°N(Songetal.,2015;Yanetal.,2017)respectively.
Hence,thenewdatasetinthisstudysupportstheLateTriassicpaleogeographicreconstructionsthathave
linkedIndochinawithNorthQiangtang(Figure3b),whichwasseriouslychallengedbythedatareported
byHuangandOpdyke(2016).

assummarizedinsection1.

blocks(Metcalfe,2013;Sengor,1987).Theglacial‐marinediamictitesinterbeddedwithmarineclasticswere
foundintheJilongFormation(P j)intheHimalaya,theLagaFormation(P l)intheGangdise,theZhanjin

5.3. ConstraintsontheEvolutionofthePaleo‐TethysOcean
ThePangeasupercontinentwasnotformeduntiltheLateCarboniferous(~320Ma)whentheGondwana
mergedwithLaurussia(Torsviketal.,2012).TheoceanicembaymentbetweenGondwanaandLaurussia
prior to the closure of the Rheic Ocean is termed the Proto‐Tethys (Stampfli & Borel, 2002). During the
Early Permian, the ocean between Gondwana and Laurussia was the originally defined Paleo‐Tethys
(Figure 3b). The North Qiangtang‐Indochina was located at approximately 22–24°S, which had already
drifted from the northern margin of Gondwana since the Early Devonian (Metcalfe, 2013). During the
Permian, different branches existed in the Paleo‐Tethys Ocean (Figure 3b). The south branch of Paleo‐
TethyshasalsobeentermedtheLongmuCo‐Shuanghu‐LancangjiangOceanbyLietal.(2016),whilethe
northbranchbetweentheNorthQiangtang‐Indochina‐SouthChinainthesouthandtheTarim‐Qaidam‐
North China in the north is termed Mianlue Ocean (Zhao et al., 2018) or Jinshajiang‐Ailaoshan Ocean
(Jianetal.,2009a,2009b;Wangetal.,2000).
DuringtheLatePermian,theNorthQiangtang‐Indochinaareinterpretedtohavebeenlocatedinequatorial
areas(Figure3c;Huangetal.,1992;Chietal.,2016;Maetal.,2019),aswellastheKarakoram(Muttonietal.,
2009).TheirbreakupwiththeSouthChinaBlockisinterpretedtobetriggedbytheeruptionoftheEmeishan
LargeIgneousProvince(Chungetal.,1998).Atthesametime,weknowlittleaboutthepositionoftheSouth
QiangtangandSibumasu(Zhaoetal.,2019),thoughtheIranianBlocksareinterpretedtohavedriftedfrom
GondwanabytheendofthePermian(Muttonietal.,2009).
BycomparingthepaleolatitudesoftheNorthQiangtangagainstthatoftheTarim‐NorthChina,Songetal.
(2015)proposedthatthenorthbranchofPaleo‐TethyshadclosedbytheLateTriassic,strictly,thelateLate
Triassic (213–204 Ma).However, the new paleolatitude estimate (26.0±4.8°N) derived from the southern
LancangjiangvolcanicbeltinthisstudyindicatesthattheNorthQiangtang‐Indochinahaddriftedfurther
northtoapproximately26°NbytheearlyLateTriassic(235–230Ma).Therefore,wesuggestthatthenorth
branchhadprobablyclosednolaterthantheearlyLateTriassic(235–230Ma;Figures3aand3d).Thiscon-
clusionisconsistentwithmuchgeologicevidence(Metcalfe,2013;Zhaoetal.,2018).Althoughtheclosureof
thesouthbranchofthePaleo‐Tethyshasnotbeenderivedfrompaleomagneticevidence,therecordofocea-
nic evolution‐related rocks including ophiolite, radiolarian chert, high‐pressure eclogite, and blueschist
indicatesthattheclosureofthesouthbranchofPaleo‐TethysverylikelyoccurredduringthelateMiddle
TriassictoearlyLateTriassic(Figure3d;Zhong,1998;Metcalfe,2013;Lietal.,2016).

6. Conclusions
WereportarobustearlyLateTriassicpaleomagneticpolewithtightageconstraintfromvolcanicrocksin
thesouthernLancangjiangvolcanicbelt.TheChRMspassfold,reversal,andespeciallyconglomeratetests
and are very likely primary thermal remanent magnetization records. The new pole (46.1°N/176.2°E,
K=44.9,A =4.8,N=21)correspondsapaleolatitudeof26.0±4.8°Natthereferencesite(23.0°N/100.4°E)
95
inthe southern Lancangjiang area.Wesuggest a close paleogeographic affinity for Indochina andNorth
QiangtangBlocks,atleastduringtheEarlyPermiantoLateTriassicinterval,andproposethatthenorth
branchofthePaleo‐TethysOceanclosednolaterthantheearlyLateTriassic.
